## The question

[Use (or redefine a) \tag command in text mode](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/13347/use-or-redefine-a-tag-command-in-text-mode), asked by user4169 on TeX Stack Exchange (2011-03-14; [CC BY-SA 2.5](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/2.5/)):

> In some times I have to set a tag in front of a text math formula. It seems better to define a command `\TAG`, as `$\TAG{Pythagoras' Equation}a^2+b^2=c^2$` to get `<Pythagoras' Equation> a^2+b^2=c^2`. The `\TAG` command need fit several conditions:
>
> 1. give a convenience to change the l(r)angle globally;
> 2. the content could be broken down, but do not at left angle;
> 3. it'd better be put in math mode.
>
> Of course the amsmath `\tag` command might be modified to suit my demand, but I don't know how to do.
>
>
> @ TH.: O.K. 
>
> 1. Think about an onerous editor who likes green color than black or a pair of parenthese than a pair of angle.
> 2. When the content of \TAG is very long, it cannot overlap the right margin, and its suitable break line point mustn't at the left delimiter as most of people want.
> 3. The command is in math mode, so it can be affected by \mathsurround, \everymath, etc.
>
> add an image
> https://i.sstatic.net/ZUgVk.png
:::

Here is a `\TAG` macro that sets its content (assumed to be text) in a parbox of a specifiable width as a tag between customizable delimiters: 

```latex
\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsmath}
\newlength{\tagwidth}
\setlength{\tagwidth}{1in}
\newcommand{\tagldelim}{\langle}
\newcommand{\tagrdelim}{\rangle}
\newcommand{\TAG}[1]{\tag*{$\left\tagldelim\parbox{\tagwidth}{#1}\right\tagrdelim$}}
\begin{document}
\[
\TAG{Pythagoras' Equation}a^2+b^2=c^2
\]
\setlength{\tagwidth}{2in}
\renewcommand{\tagrdelim}{\rbrack}
\[
\TAG{Theory of life, the universe, and everything}
6 \times 9 = 42
\]
\end{document}
```
